title: Subdiaphragmatic Vagotomy
author: Kavi Rude
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bfhdjj26

steps.title: Induce Anesthesia
steps.instruction: Place the mouse in the induction chamber, close the lid, and deliver isoflurane and O2 via stopcock valves.

substeps.instruction: Monitor for slower respiratory rate, loss of balance, and slowed movement.
Remove mouse from chamber after approximately 3 minutes when recumbent and non-responsive.

steps.title: Maintain Anesthesia and Position Mouse
steps.instruction: Place the mouse in dorsal recumbency on the shaving station pad and maintain anesthesia using a nose cone.

substeps.instruction: Redirect Isoflurane and O2 flow to the nose cone and close access to the induction chamber.
If necessary, secure the nose with a suture strap under the front central incisors tied to the nose cone.

steps.title: Prepare Surgical Site
steps.instruction: Protect the eyes and clear the surgical area of hair.

substeps.instruction: Apply ample sterile eye lubricant to each eye.
Use a charged shaver to remove hair from the underside, starting between the hypogastrium and umbilical region and shaving rostrally to the xiphoid process.
Brush off excess hair with a q-tip.

steps.title: Secure Mouse for Surgery
steps.instruction: Transfer the mouse to the surgical area beneath the scope while keeping the head in the nose cone.

substeps.instruction: Secure forelimbs to the absorbent pad using tape 'cuffs' so arms are perpendicular to the body.
Secure the tail with tape.

steps.title: Verify Anesthesia Depth
steps.instruction: Monitor the mouse for appropriate anesthesia depth using a toe-pinch stimulus.

substeps.instruction: Ensure respirations remain rhythmic and slowed.
Increase isoflurane if fast respiratory rate, spontaneous movement, or response to toe-pinch occurs.
Decrease isoflurane if respiratory rate becomes markedly slower or the animal gasps.

steps.title: Sterilize and Drape
steps.instruction: Clean the incision site and apply a sterile drape.

substeps.instruction: Clean the site first with alcohol and then chlorhexidine, wiping in a spiral from the center outward.
Allow prepping solution to dry completely.
Secure a pre-cut, autoclaved paper towel drape over the animal, ensuring breathing can still be monitored.

steps.title: Perform Abdominal Incision
steps.instruction: Create a two-stage midline incision from the umbilicus to approximately 0.5cm below the xiphoid process.

substeps.instruction: First incision: Cut through skin, subcutaneous tissue, and fascia (max length ~1.5cm for males, ~1.25cm for females).
Separate skin from abdominal cavity lining by inserting closed scissors between layers and gently opening blades, angling away from the body cavity.
Second incision: Cut through the linea alba, transversalis fascia, and peritoneum lining, angling scissors away from the viscera.

steps.title: Expose the Esophagus
steps.instruction: Clear the surgical field to visualize the esophageal insertion at the stomach.

substeps.instruction: Use a Q-tip to gently push viscera (intestines) down into the hypogastric region.
Lift the left and median lobes of the liver to expose the stomach edge.
Hook the esophagus and guide the stomach medially to align the esophagus with the incision.

steps.title: Isolate and Resect Vagus Nerve
steps.instruction: Identify and cut the vagus nerve at the esophageal hiatus.

substeps.instruction: Follow the esophagus to the esophageal hiatus.
Use sharpened 45-degree angled forceps to grab the vagus nerve as close to the diaphragm as possible (remove thin fascial sheath if necessary).
If the nerve is hard to find, gently rotate the esophagus clockwise using the hook.
Peel the vagus nerve off the esophagus and use micro scissors to cut the vagal insertion at the base of the esophagus.

steps.title: Internal Organ Restoration
steps.instruction: Restore and verify the position of internal organs.

substeps.instruction: Return the stomach, liver lobes, and intestines to their original positions.
Examine internal organ orientation to ensure all organs are intact and correctly placed.

steps.title: Close the Incision
steps.instruction: Suture the abdominal wall and staple the skin.

substeps.instruction: Close the linea alba: Use one cruciate suture if the incision is ≤1cm; otherwise, use simple interrupted sutures spaced 2-3mm apart.
Free the skin from remaining fascia using scissors to ensure the skin is loose.
Bring skin seams together like a tent using forceps.
Place staples with a space of about half a staple width between each; use forceps or needle driver to tighten if needed.
If skin puckers at the end, apply a line of suture to seal.

steps.title: Post-Operative Recovery
steps.instruction: Place the mouse in a recovery cage and monitor until fully awake.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a recovery cage with a heating pad under one half of the cage only, using a clean paper towel as a barrier (do not use bedding).
Place the animal in ventral or lateral recumbency.
Monitor the mouse in the procedure room until it has completely recovered.
Return the animal to its home cage once it can walk freely and shows appropriate alertness and responsivity.
